content: Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or pharmacological effects of imatinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, ketoconazole enhances imatinib levels through inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Clinical caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole elevates the levels or effects of imipramine by interfering with CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Careful monitoring is recommended. Ketoconazole increases the systemic levels of indacaterol (inhaled) by modulating both P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and CYP3A4 activities. No dose adjustment is necessary at the 75 mcg dose, but caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole enhances the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal formulations by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Clinical caution and monitoring are necessary. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Ketoconazole elevates the levels or effects of istradefylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The istradefylline dose should not exceed 20 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Clinical caution and monitoring are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Ivacaftor dosage should be reduced when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. Ketoconazole enhances the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Clinical caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels of lacosamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Patients with renal or hepatic impairment taking strong CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 inhibitors may experience significant increases in lacosamide exposure, necessitating dose reduction. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Both ketoconazole and lapatinib prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole elevates the levels or effects of lesinurad (DSC) by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Ketoconazole enhances the effects of letermovir by reducing its metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Letermovir increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating monitoring. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine, potentially requiring dose reduction. Monitor for hypotension and edema symptoms to determine dose adjustments. Ketoconazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The levomilnacipran dose should not exceed 80 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. Nonhormonal contraceptive use is recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of linagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Ketoconazole enhances the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitoring and caution are necessary. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole doses exceeding 200 mg/day are not recommended when used with lopinavir/ritonavir. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Ketoconazole elevates the levels or effects of losartan by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This may inhibit the conversion of losartan to its active metabolite E-3174. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear; individual therapeutic response should be monitored to determine losartan dosage. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitoring and caution are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Due to lumacaftor's CYP3A induction effect, net ivacaftor exposure at steady state is not expected to exceed monotherapy levels. No dose adjustment is needed when initiating CYP3A inhibitors in patients on lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when starting lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients on strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week to allow for lumacaftor's induction effect. Resume the recommended daily dose thereafter. No adjustment is needed for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The lumateperone dose should not exceed 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitoring and caution are necessary. The maraviroc dose should be reduced to 150 mg BID when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole elevates the levels or effects of marijuana by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor mavorixafor levels when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors and reduce the dose if necessary. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are recommended. Ketoconazole enhances the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitoring and caution are necessary. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitoring and caution are advised. Ketoconazole and mipomersen both increase each other's toxicity due to their potential to elevate hepatic enzymes. Liver function tests (LFTs) should be monitored. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the mirtazapine dose if co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary. Consider increasing the dose once the inhibitor is discontinued. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of mirvetuximab soravtansine, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Ketoconazole elevates the levels or effects of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are necessary. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of mometasone (inhaled and intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised due to the increased risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitoring and caution are necessary. Monitor for potential adverse effects when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Ketoconazole elevates the levels or effects of nateglinide by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Nefazodone increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ketoconazole also raises nefazodone levels through the same mechanism. Monitoring and caution are required. Ketoconazole enhances the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitoring and caution are necessary. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of neomycin (oral) by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitoring and caution are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are recommended. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, but no dosage adjustment is required. Ketoconazole elevates the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are necessary. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of nifedipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitoring and caution are recommended. Ketoconazole enhances the levels or effects of nimodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are necessary. Ketoconazole raises the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If adverse effects occur, management may involve therapy interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation. Nirmatrelvir increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Limit ketoconazole doses to 200 mg/day when co-administered with ritonavir. Ketoconazole elevates the levels or effects of nitrendipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are necessary. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic norgestrel concentrations, raising the risk of adverse effects. Ketoconazole and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dose until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. CYP450 inhibitors may reduce ondansetron clearance, but no dosage adjustment is recommended. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Ketoconazole elevates the levels of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are necessary. Ketoconazole raises the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Oxycodone dose reduction may be necessary when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole enhances the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and caution are recommended.
